meaning:
σβέννυμι
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבָה ;]
of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, Mat.12:20, Eph.6:16, Heb.11:34; pass., Mat.25:8, Mrk.9:48, [44, 46]. Metaphorical (cf. Sng.8:7, 4Ma.16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, 1Th.5:19.†
ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, 1Th.5:19 T (see WH, Notes, 148).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a smoking flax, until he leads justice to victory.
‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
above all, taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one.
quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, from weakness were made strong, grew mighty in war, and caused foreign armies to flee.
